transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Julia Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (OpalWave VP Product), Ethan Cole (OpalWave ML Eng), Priya Singh (OpalWave CTO), Liam O'Connor (OpalWave SRE)

[00:00] Samir Patel: alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync, I know we have 52 on the calendar so we can go a little over if needed. quick objective: review this week's pilot economics, caching numbers, and set action items.

[00:18] Marta Ruiz: thanks Samir. high level, the product team wants to make sure the cost numbers we showed last week are repeatable under day-to-day traffic. also want clarity on the dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for security.

[00:32] Julia Chen: great. i pulled the test runs from yesterday—the synthetic load that mirrors your conversational flow—and ran three configs: no cache, prefix cache enabled, and full KV cache hot-path. i'll share the sheet after. quick headline: prefix caching saved about 18% tokens/sec-dollar on our typical 1.2k token convo, while KV cache gave up to 28% savings for sessions with repeated context.

[00:58] Ethan Cole: those are promising numbers. Can you remind us what you mean by tokens/sec-dollar? is that raw tokens per GPU hour normalized to dollars?

[01:07] Julia Chen: yes so it's effectively tokens processed per second normalized by cost of the GPU instance per second—we combine throughput with per-hour cost to get a tokens-per-dollar figure. it's a practical metric for unit economics across model variants.

[01:22] Priya Singh: we ran a small AB test yesterday using your hosted endpoint and saw similar relative wins for caching, but our latency tail sometimes spiked when batching kicked in. anything to note there?

[01:34] Julia Chen: yeah that's the batching tradeoff—if you push larger batch sizes to improve tokens/sec you'd lower unit cost, but the tail latency especially p95..p99 can climb because a slow request in the batch delays others. In your config, the median latency was fine, but p99 jumped from ~260ms to ~720ms when we increased target batch to 8.

[01:59] Liam O'Connor: that p99 is concerning for user experience. our SLO is 400ms p95 for interactive flows, p99 ideally under 800ms but we prefer lower. are there batching knobs to mitigate tail behavior?

[02:12] Julia Chen: yes, two practical levers—dynamic batch shaping with deadlines (we cut batches when oldest waiting request hits X ms) and small-batch fast-path for short sequences. also hybrid routing: latency-critical routes skip batching and go to smaller instances or reserved capacity.

[02:29] Samir Patel: to add, Redwood Dedicated gives you the ability to pin a pool with lower variance which reduces tail amplification, but that comes with cost commitments—so it's a cost vs predictability decision.

[02:45] Marta Ruiz: can you give a concrete example of the economics? like tokens/sec-dollar delta between hosted and dedicated for our workload?

[02:53] Julia Chen: for your traffic shape—shorter sessions, many re-uses—the hosted runs we did using a mixed 70/30 gen/emb model profile showed tokens/sec-dollar of ~1,900 in hosted baseline; with prefix caching we hit ~2,250; with dedicated and KV cache on a reserved A100-like pool we measured ~2,650. numbers are sensitive to utilization—these were at ~60% avg utilization.

[03:21] Ethan Cole: good to know. how reliable are those KV numbers under eviction? in prod our sessions are long and caches might have churn.

[03:29] Julia Chen: that's a great callout. the savings degrade as you increase cache miss rate. i ran an eviction sweep where we raised unique context churn to 3x and saw KV benefit fall from 28% to about 9%—prefix caching remained more stable. we'll run a longer tail test for you.

[03:47] Priya Singh: that matches our intuition—so maybe we should rely primarily on prefix caching and treat KV as an incremental optimization if we can control affinity.

[03:56] Samir Patel: sounds reasonable. Another variable is quantization: we tested int8 low-precision variant last week and saw about 22% cost improvement but the hallucination rate nudged up on a couple prompts. we can show a per-scenario quality delta so you can decide.

[04:12] Marta Ruiz: yes quality impact is a blocker for customer-facing summaries. can we gate quantized models to internal only, or maybe run an A/B with fallback?

[04:20] Julia Chen: absolutely. Redwood supports rollout policies—canary by user segment and fallback to FP16 if triggers detect quality degradation, and we can log examples to your secure audit bucket for review.

[04:33] Ethan Cole: quick operational question—if we go private (VPC), does the cost profile change materially? our infra team is concerned about egress and instance pricing.

[04:43] Samir Patel: private deployments shift some costs (you might supply infra or we bill for private nodes). typically tokens/sec-dollar on identical hardware is similar, but management overhead and reserved instance pricing vary. we can model both scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[04:58] Liam O'Connor: about security—Priya and i reviewed SOC2 and SSO docs. we need to confirm KMS integration for key wrapping before infra signs off. timeline?

[05:08] Julia Chen: we have KMS/HSM options documented—i'll surface the private deployment security package and KMS integration playbook in the shared folder.

[05:16] Marta Ruiz: earlier you mentioned sudden drops in throughput during a GC-like event on the runtime—we saw an incident last week where throughput dipped 30% for ~10 minutes. any root cause?

[05:26] Julia Chen: that was an artifact of our KV cache compaction combined with a model kernel swap on the node. we've rolled a patch that staggers compaction and ensures kernel swaps happen during lower load windows; we haven't seen recurrence in the last 48h. we'll keep monitoring.

[05:40] Ethan Cole: can you run a 4-hour degradation test where we ramp unique session churn so we can observe when KV benefits fall off? we'd like to see the breakpoint.

[05:47] Julia Chen: yes i can do that and include perf counters (latency distribution, cache hit ratio, GPU util) and we'll annotate the logs.

[05:53] Samir Patel: action item: i'll update the unit-econ spreadsheet to include three scenarios—no cache, prefix cache, and prefix+KV with hit-rate sensitivity curves. i'll include hosted vs dedicated pricing buckets and show tokens/sec-dollar and median/p99 latency impacts.

[06:08] Marta Ruiz: timeline for that?

[06:10] Samir Patel: i'll send by 2026-12-24. Julia will send the KV stress test logs by 2026-12-28. Ethan to provide a 7-day traffic trace by 2026-12-27.

[06:22] Priya Singh: one more ask—can we have a short session with your infra folks on quantization pitfalls and how you detect quality regressions? maybe Jan 4th?

[06:30] Julia Chen: yes we can set that up. propose a 60m deep-dive, we'll invite performance and model ops.

[06:36] Samir Patel: ok to recap and close: 1) Samir sends pricing sheet with scenario modeling (due 12/24), 2) Julia runs KV eviction test and shares logs (due 12/28), 3) Ethan exports traffic traces (due 12/27), 4) schedule quantization deep-dive week of Jan 4th.

[06:53] Marta Ruiz: sounds good, thanks everyone. last question—any immediate blockers to continuing the pilot through end of Jan?

[07:02] Priya Singh: none on our side, wants security sign-off but that's a parallel path.

[07:08] Samir Patel: perfect. we'll follow up in email with links to the dashboard and spreadsheet. thanks all.

[07:15] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has generic ASR noise—some product names transcribed as "A 100" or "A100 like pool". references to URLs and docs were mentioned; links to the shared drive and pricing workbook will be included in follow-up email.
